# What I Owe the Board

Sunday thinking before the Oct 21 board meeting. Engineering section of the deck is due Oct 17. Writing what I actually think first, so the deck doesn't write it for me.

## The temptation

The deck wants to say: we closed a term sheet ($38M at $210M post, Northfield leading, Granite Peak pro-rata), we rebuilt ACH with zero missed cutoffs since Aug 18, MAU is 151k, investing beta is live. All true.

What it doesn't want to say: we had a SEV1 on Sep 26 that double-debited 1,412 users, investing GA is at risk for Oct 20, SOC 2 has three open gaps in the middle of a Type II window, and the CTO is the single point of failure for about half of the company's decisions.

Dana will have read the postmortem. Ravi's diligence advisor will have read it too. If I lead with the good news, the bad news shows up as a question. If I lead with the bad news, it shows up as an answer.

## What I owe them

1. **The truth about Sep 26, in the first five minutes.** What happened, why the new pipeline wasn't involved, why that's not reassuring (we knew the sweep job was outside it), and what we're doing: idempotency keys on every money-moving job by Oct 23, the sweep onto the outbox pipeline in Q4, a written remediation plan to Pillar by Oct 15.
2. **A real GA risk read.** Not "on track." Three blockers on Sep 29, one closed since (disclosures signed Oct 7), two open. Go/no-go #2 on Oct 16. If it's a no-go, I'd rather say so on Oct 21 than spin it.
3. **SOC 2 status as numbers.** Access review 70%, vendor risk 2 of 4, MDM 96%. Dates for each. Northfield asked for a status letter; the board should see the same facts.
4. **Key-person risk, named.** Me and Marcus. The VP Eng decision lands by Oct 20, and I want the board to hear the plan for what moves off both of us ([[Stop Being the Router]]).
5. **What the money is for.** 12 engineering hires in 9 months, and why that order. Burn is $540k/month, runway 15 months before the round. Their money buys time; I owe them a plan that spends it on the things that broke.

## What I don't owe them

Performance of confidence. Aleks carries the narrative; my job is the truth ([[Walking Thoughts - Series B]] said this in May, and it's still right). They funded a company, not a mood.

## The question I'm scared they'll ask

"Two money-movement incidents in six months. Why should we believe the third won't happen?"

Honest answer: I can't promise it won't. I can show that the first one made us build reconciliation, and reconciliation is what caught the second one in 47 minutes instead of on Monday. That's the actual improvement. Not "no incidents." Faster, smaller, owned.
